posts.content_html_raw:
You know, for a self-confessed awful human being, the MC is getting deeply involved in the lives of all of these girls, isn't he?

I mean, it's funny... Well, not funny. But it's interesting, how much I've gotten sucked into all of these painful stories, quite separate from the see-girl-fuck-girl pattern of most h games (which Selebus teases us with very kindly). Sana, Rin, Futaba, Chika... Maya... Maya. I may be wrong, but I get the sense that the MC did something really awful to her in the first "life" that kicked off this hellish temporal loop/NO EXIT hell. What that was — whether he raped her, or betrayed her, or killed her, or killed/raped/betrayed her best friend Ami, or what, I don't know. She clearly knows him really, really well, though he's grown enough to surprise her occasionally. But as we go along, between her odd moments of candor and the wildly surreal, creepy-as-fuck "happy" scenes, I'm finding her bitterness toward Sensei more and more moving. And yeah — I think of Coraline too every time I see those eyes. :shudder:

Not sure what the end game here is. Not sure whether this is a one-way descent into hell/madness or there's a nirvanic escape hatch somewhere along the line. But I'm fascinated to see where it goes.

That I'll break someone's heart, betray someone's trust, let someone down when they need me most.

And I should be. That's life. Sometimes your decisions have consequences you can't predict, and sometimes they hurt the people you care about most. posts.content_html_raw:
Just finished the beach scene and most of the events.

I forgot whether or not the forced kiss thing with Yumi was something the player was given a choice on, or if it's something that just happens regardless of player actions.

Anyway, will there actually be H-scenes with Yumi and Maya in the future? Or are those two just simply unobtainable? They both seem to be unobtainable forever, especially Maya. The story made me very interested in how a route with her would play out.

Also, I'm getting some Undertale vibes with this game. At least the pervert-teacher equivalent; assuming one can play the game either as a the worst person, or a relatively more decent person compared with the former option, will certain actions permanently effect the game even if you start a whole new game?

Anyway, I have to give the games two thumbs up. When I first downloaded, I completely failed to notice the "loli" and "horror" tags, neither of which I would have touched with a ten foot pole (especially the loli tag.) The horror elements were a huge shock, but they drew me in. The writing overall is good enough to get me over just how awful playing a protagonist going after a bunch of fifteen-sixteen year olds would make me feel. I'm hungry for the truth behind the room with clocks,

and to find out what's buried underneath my feet.

Can someone point me to the meaning of different colours of girls names,that we can see in AFFection!?
Click to expand...
No particular meaning. It just makes identifying the characters easier.

Their names also appear in those colors when they talk. You might be able to look into some color theory to see how the color might apply to them, but it's mostly just to help you identify who's talking while only seeing the name in your peripheral vision. That's why the color often corresponds to their hair color, a primary color they wear, or is close to a color they wear. Since those colors get associated with them more easily.

posts.content_html_raw:
goodhomie = undo betraying Rin.

rosebud = increases affection with all girls by 100.

lagfix = resets the call stack which an early version of the headpat system caused to pile up and cause lag. Doesn't mark save as a cheater.

floor1victory = make it so floor 1 won the dorm war.

floor2victory = make it so floor 2 won the dorm war.

dormwartie = make it so the dorm war resulted in a tie.

funinthesun = resets the beach event and makes it trigger the next Sunday.

fingeryourniece = resets Ami's events 'No One Can See Us' and 'Important Things' and gives the message "You now have the opportunity to be a better uncle." Guessing there's gonna be consequences to these events in the future.
This cheat only works if you haven't completed the Christmas event yet (specifically the event named "Fireworks, Chicken, and the Innate Fear of Death"). Attempting to use it after the Christmas event does nothing, not even marking your save as a cheater.
If your playing the censored version, replace the word niece in the cheat with whatever the censor replaces it with. I've never played it, but the cheat is set up to accept the alternative.

iwillalwaysloveyou = increase Ami's lust by 100.

bubblewrapprincess = increase Ayane's lust by 100.

likemotherlikedaughter = increase Makoto's lust by 100.

heartofgold = increase Chika's lust by 100.

atreefallsintheforest = increase Futaba's lust by 100.

supermom = increase Sara's lust by 100.

thouartsick = increase Haruka's lust by 100.

youonlyliveonce = increase Kirin's lust by 100.

openrelationship = increase Maki's lust by 100.

shiningstar = increase Niki's lust by 100.

seemeafterclass = count Chika's 'Detention' lust event as having triggered.

wheredoesthetimego = "100 Days pass while you sit at the computer. It's almost like real life now, isn't it?"
That last line is straight out of the game. I thought it was funny enough to just copy/paste.
Using any of these cheat codes except the few noted will silently mark your save as a cheater. As of version 0.22.0 there are no repercussions to using these cheats. However, this is a denpa game (see horror tag). As such, there is a very real chance some very bad consequences will be implemented in the future for cheating. I recommend playing without cheats first, then, if it's too much of a grind, using a save editor instead of these cheats.
Cheats are entered using the "Computer" option on the weekend.

The power dynamic between Sensei and Ami's relationship is too one sided for it to develop into a proper romantic relationship. This will likely result in a really unhealthy relationship down the line.
Finally, part of the reason she does all those things to Sensei is because she has some pretty major parental issues. Ami doesn't need to get laid. She needs professional help.
Don't get me wrong. This shit is hot AF and I have gotten off to it. But it's still good to keep context for why these things are generally looked down upon in real life. Consent isn't the issue here.
[Edit]
In terms of videogame logic, you're right. There are absolutely no points that say that having sex with Ami is the wrong choice or something bad to do. But that's kind of the point. Both us and Sensei see decisions in these games as only having short term minor consequences which can easily, or semi-easily, be undone while mostly being motivated by our libidos and/or desire to see more of the story/characters. However, a common theme in denpa games like this is to apply real world logic to the decisions made in them and treating the characters as if they're real people to show how messed up using that videogame logic can be.
[/Edit]

In my opinion, every 'version' of LiL should have a little bit of each element that players have gotten used to over the last seven months.

And Part 2 would have something like: Girl Events, Lust Events, UI Improvements
I'd feel like I was cheating people passing off two weeks of work as an entire version of the game, so I decided to split it into two different parts.

posts.content_html_raw: So I finally got around to playing my original save through all of Rin's events and the beach scene from the bad homie perspective, making this the first time I've watched a large chunk of events in full because I stopped right in the middle of Chika's Detention event once I realized I forgot that my save was no good for an all girl run as it was originally intended for. This also marks the second time I have gone through the beach event as I usually reserve the second play through for the full game. Normally, with anything fiction, I put up emotional barriers and try to play it from a completely logical standpoint, something that I have never succeeded in with this game, but it not only broke those barriers once, it has broken them every time so far. It actually hurt to watch Rin break down like that even after knowing exactly what happens and it hurt worse knowing I was the cause of her pain. Not many works of fiction can do that to me, maybe 15 total from all mediums combined. I've come to realize that this game isn't good, it isn't great....it's absolutely amazing, among the top 5 games of its type that I have played and that list is multiple pages long at this point. This is a true work of art you have going Selebus and I really mean that. I might even be able to call it a masterpiece. I think you've more than earned my support with that scene alone, so I will be considering it in a few days, when the next month kicks in.

It doesn't have to and I'm not sure Sensei deserves it, granted I might be channeling a bit of post rejection Rin right now, more like a hypothetical version of her that didn't just let what Sensei did to her love interest slide and actually got visibly pissed at him for it, so I might be more than a little biased on that. Ngl, I've hated that kind of thinking for a while now. It's obviously just differing philosophies and I'll probably use some extreme examples but I've never understood why people enjoy that sort of thing.

It's the kind of thing where I never enjoy stories where if I know the main character/heroine ends up dying at the end or something. I don't like stories that have all the happy moments and struggles throughout the middle only to have a bitter ending. I'd rather take an empty one/open ended one instead.

I personally wouldn't mind extreme exaggerated suffering if I knew I would end up at a good place. After all, what's the point of living all happy and such to just have it taken away from you in the end?

I like Re:Zero a lot for example, the journey is horrible, excruciating, and hard to watch at times. It makes me appreciate Subaru more as a character, not many would do the things he would. He goes through the hardship just because he wants everyone else to be happy- He himself might not have a happy ending at the end but he's damned himself to at least make sure everyone else does.

So I really wouldn't mind if there's an extremely hard to reach ending for this game if just to give all the characters a bit of happiness at the end- Cause screw the journey if everyone else just ends up sad.

TL;DR: I'll take a shitty painful journey over a nice one as long as the girls end up happy. Selebus pls

I like Re:Zero a lot for example, the journey is horrible, excruciating, and hard to watch at times. It makes me appreciate Subaru more as a character, not many would do the things he would. So I really wouldn't mind if there's an extremely hard to reach ending for this game if just to give all the characters a bit of happiness at the end- Cause screw the journey if everyone else just ends up sad.

I'll take a shitty painful journey over a nice one as long as the girls end up happy.

This post is pretty bad at explaining exactly what I was trying to get across and is painting with a very broad brush. iwassnow does a much better job of explaining APD in his post below, since I'm quite ignorant about it. To keep from making some bad generalizations, please read through it.
iwassnow said:
Hey there! I'm coming back from my otherwise mute lurking to dispel something here. Antisocial personality disorder does not mean you don't feel anything for others(ie lack empathy). That's sociopathy(which is a rare subset of APD). APD, that I have, means you have a difficult time communicating and/or understanding feelings(it's a broad diagnosis that covers many actual behaviors). In my personal case, I have a difficult time expressing my own emotions to others for a lack of ability to communicate them in a way that my listener understands(as opposed to a lack of understanding of my own feelings myself which can also be APD).

Sociopathy, that a friend of mine has, is primarily identified by a lack of empathy and an inability to show legitimate feelings towards others(as well as manipulation to conceal that behavior). This also is very specific in that it doesn't mean you don't have emotions, but rather your emotional spectrum is narrow. For my friend, he does an excellent job of being a decent human being, and as a rarity does not lie to others that his behavior is an act(he explained to me that he knows how he is is wrong, and so he's trying his best to make up for it while being honest; most sociopaths aren't like this).

Sensei however likely does have APD but not sociopathy, because his contradictory internal monologues seem to alude to other feelings but his response to himself seem to be to immediately bury those feelings. That's reminisce of a conditioned response, and people with such behavior usually lack emotional intelligence. They don't understand their own feelings, and how they react to them can be widely different from person to person. In my own case, when I was younger, APD for me meant I also did not understand myself. Years of therapy, research, and trying to grow up later, I'm able to at least understand myself.

So the thing I should clarify here and the reason I wrote this wall of text was in defense of that man you met. While sociopathy is a form of APD, it is usually not what most diagnosis mean. And while I cannot speak for him spefically(because maybe he does have sociopathy), I don't want others to make a wrong assumption and believe that all persons with APD don't feel empathy towards others. We do, and in fact, often more strongly than the average person which is contributory to our difficulties with handling them.

And since I know I have difficulty with communicating my own emotions, I'm going to robotically state that the above was meant to only be educational and clarifying, not confrontational(your statement wasn't wrong, but its lack of context would easily create misleading perceptions). So I hope I didn't come off as offensive or rude. :S

Hey there! I'm coming back from my otherwise mute lurking to dispel something here. Antisocial personality disorder does not mean you don't feel anything for others(ie lack empathy). That's sociopathy(which is a rare subset of APD). APD, that I have, means you have a difficult time communicating and/or understanding feelings(it's a broad diagnosis that covers many actual behaviors). In my personal case, I have a difficult time expressing my own emotions to others for a lack of ability to communicate them in a way that my listener understands(as opposed to a lack of understanding of my own feelings myself which can also be APD).

Sociopathy, that a friend of mine has, is primarily identified by a lack of empathy and an inability to show legitimate feelings towards others(as well as manipulation to conceal that behavior). This also is very specific in that it doesn't mean you don't have emotions, but rather your emotional spectrum is narrow. For my friend, he does an excellent job of being a decent human being, and as a rarity does not lie to others that his behavior is an act(he explained to me that he knows how he is is wrong, and so he's trying his best to make up for it while being honest; most sociopaths aren't like this).

Sensei however likely does have APD but not sociopathy, because his contradictory internal monologues seem to alude to other feelings but his response to himself seem to be to immediately bury those feelings. That's reminisce of a conditioned response, and people with such behavior usually lack emotional intelligence. They don't understand their own feelings, and how they react to them can be widely different from person to person. In my own case, when I was younger, APD for me meant I also did not understand myself. Years of therapy, research, and trying to grow up later, I'm able to at least understand myself.

So the thing I should clarify here and the reason I wrote this wall of text was in defense of that man you met. While sociopathy is a form of APD, it is usually not what most diagnosis mean. And while I cannot speak for him spefically(because maybe he does have sociopathy), I don't want others to make a wrong assumption and believe that all persons with APD don't feel empathy towards others. We do, and in fact, often more strongly than the average person which is contributory to our difficulties with handling them.

And since I know I have difficulty with communicating my own emotions, I'm going to robotically state that the above was meant to only be educational and clarifying, not confrontational(your statement wasn't wrong, but its lack of context would easily create misleading perceptions). So I hope I didn't come off as offensive or rude. :S

posts.content_html_raw:
I don't know if this has been said before here, but I hope the dev has a concrete idea for how the story and happy events will play out and isn't making it up as they go along. While i have no reason to doubt their creativity and improvisation, a careful plan would probably result in higher quality.

If i had to give my criticism, it would be that the direction the event design is taking means that in a few major updates i will no longer be able to figure things out when it comes to mutually exclusive choices and hard-to-find stuff, and will have to resort to this forum or a walkthrough to see everything the game has to offer.

Thus far this has been an incredibly interesting and engaging experience. Couldn't care less if it had no pornographic content, even though i also couldn't imagine it without it since it is (mostly) integral to the plot.

I truly wish that the dev makes more games after this project is done, and that the mystifying nature they've maintained here will find its way in their future works.

posts.content_html_raw:
Here's my personal archive of everything i could find in the happy events. Be warned that the formatting is terrible, as it wasn't meant for others' viewing, but i hope at least someone is interested in it, since i don't think i could ever find the more obscure stuff. I only added a couple more comments and some extra lines to make it barely readable.

Secret events are in order of appearance in memories / scene replay. After the event's number, secrets are in order of appearance inside the event.

1 - Name of girl : am i okay (Hex to text) (61 6d 20 69 20 6f 6b 61 79 , it reappears in many other scenes)
Japanese (っかれた。) : i was taken. (google translate)​
Japanese (こんばんは。) : Good evening. (google translate)​
Chinese (笑) : Laughter (google translate)​
Japanese (あ) : Ahhhhh (google translate)​
REcoorDinating has the RED letters capitalized​

2 - The text-to-speech voice calls out some words. Initials spell out AGAIN SHE LIVES (and says "The answer you seek is hope")
Door : hope (Hex to text)​
Japanese : (私を破壊する) = Destroy me​
(希望は答えではない) = Hope is not the answer​
(ワナだ) = It's a trap​
(生きたい。。。) = Want to live...​
(助けて。) = help.​
Second to last line in event : there is no hope (Hex to text)​

3 - Couldn't find anything here. The last screen says "where are we" and a couple other obvious phrases. May be worth looking into it more.

4 - Japanese (こんにちは) : Hello
Japanese (普通の女子高生。) : An ordinary school girl.​
Japanese (望む) : Want. (?) Full sentence : "Feed him to 望む!" , want seems to not fit?​
Japanese (あなたなしで毎日。。。) : Every day without you...​
Chinese (笑) : Laughter​
Flashing image : We are all gone and there is nothing​
Your name in hex : sekai (Hex to text​
Japanese (あ) : Ahhhhh​
Father's name : hope (Hex to text)​
​
"amiokay"'s speech if you pick "no" :​
​
"but i have waited so long"​
"why are you doing this to me"​
"just fuck me"​
"i miss it"​
"i want to feel you inside"​
"i want to remember"​

5 - Some dialogue is backwards but i didn't find anything important in it
Japanese (どういう意味) : What do you mean (Shows up twice)​

6 - Japanese (あなたは誰) : Who are you
(だれ です か) : Who​

Text on flashing screen : do you remember the first time you told me you told me you loved me? it was snowing. i was wearing a green scarf. i confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. when you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. like everything i've ever wanted was finally mine. and i could finally be happy. you took me to your room and took my panties off. you put your fingers inside me and i started crying. but they were happy tears - because i finally knew what it meant to be loved. (This is from a series of pictures that flash during one of Ami's lust events. Don't know if it is a reference to something else, or if it is important to the plot)​
​
Japanese (世界) : world (amiokay/Maya calls you that, connects with sekai being your name in event #4)​
Random words form with initials : RAISE YOUR HEAD (i can recognize albatross and iodine repeating from before)​
​
Lots of Hex to text comes next. All of it on the blackboard in the flashing images. Everything between "..." is plain text.​
Translation in position of appearance :​
I see more in the dark so many​
but i still can't see you wonderful things​
remember this place cuddled up​
if it's the last thing you do beside you​
"list the things you love am i among them?" "and not one single twin stop looking for answers"​
​
You can also see japanese posters on the background in some images, but they don't appear to be related (untranslated).​

7 - Japanese (おかえり) : Welcome back
Text-to-speech voice plays AGAIN SHE LIVES

Hex to text dialogue :​
an echo rings out in the distance​
It sounds something like a school bell​
But it's not one I'm familiar with​
For some reason, deep in the back of my mind​
I remember something​
It's a green scarf​
And the arms of the only person to have ever truly loved me​
​
(There's the green scarf thing again. Maybe it connects to something else and i'm blind. Also, more dialogue (in plain text) about throwing into the wishing well.)​

8 - As other girls appear in the hallway, game says "The room fills with wonderful things" (plaintext) and Ami repeats the
blackboard's words verbatim. Definitely what the blackboard was talking about in #6.​
Ami also calls you her "world" multiple times.​
White cat?​



9 - Spanish (El clima es rojo) - The weather is red
23 layers in hell.​
Voiceover : "Beneath you lies a promising future", "wires", God in second part of town?,​
"Kill the caloused one/god, kill the concerned" (Maya says not to pick the caloused god if gods exist in #8​
Music/voiceover is called godishere.​
​
Text in Caesar's cipher +7​
Sensei : who are you and why does this place burn my skin​
can you tell me the way to get home​
how do you know that​
are you me​
God(?)/HOPE : THERE IS ONLY ONE GOD​
WHICH ONE WILL YOU CHOOSE​
THERE ARE TWO WRONG ANSWERS​
​
HOPE mentions someone else with wires and wires...​
Grave message : hope have (Hex to text) (?) Maybe reading it wrong.​
Red text on screen : againshelives (Caesar's shift +7)​
Music is called amiawake in this part (and is quite pleasant)​

I know this isn't everything in the game, as there's some stuff that connects in the
beach
event, and there could easily be more in the files/pictures. Maybe i'll have a look after i finish playing through the update.

Here's the text during the 2 "important" parts in the halloween event. It's not hard to find or read them, but just for convenience's sake i'll paste it here, in case it hasn't been yet.

Halloween is in script.rpy

Text in chicken date (Kaori) Screen name howtowish :
What did you want to be when you were little? I bet it was something fun like and astronaut or a policeman. What you didn't want to be, though, was someone who grows up alone. Someone who sits in their room each night, staring at the wall and wishing to be absorbed by it. Swallowed whole, even. What your parents should have told you when you came to them with that dream is that dreams do not come true unless you are willing to go to extremes to obtain them. They will not come true unless you change the world to fit your desires. I worry about you, you know? I'm very concerned. I think about you almost constantly. Never in a sexual manner or anything like that, just a normal manner. I consider us friends. You and I have always been friends, haven't we? Do you remember the nights you used to talk to me before going to sleep? How you'd tell me all of your problems and I'd just sit there listening? Those were some of my favorite nights of all. But you never told me about those dreams or how you wanted to be an astronaut. You only told me the bad things. How family members were sick or how you were afraid of failing a test. Things like that. Why don't you ever tell me anything happy? Why don't you ever thank me for being there for you? I give you everything. I hear your voice as if it's my own. It is my own. I REALLY like this game. The girls are beautiful, the scenes are really good, and the story line is great.

I only have ONE major problem with this game:

The lack of a walkthrough, the GOD awful amount of grind that I have to go through to open up events, the LACK of hints in the event tracker (or the inability to open hints in how to get the events),And the convoluted steps needed to go through just to advance the damned story.

Because of this problem I find that I may have to discontinue and delete this game. Don't get me wrong, but damn, it would be nice if you had a hint system in place. Even THAT would go far in making this game worth playing. Consider this my suggestion for how to improve the play-ability of this game.

Otherwise, VERY nice game and love the frequency of updates.

Ok so I had to stop my first playthrough to talk about this game.

I like it, but I'm super conflicted and I don't think it's in the way I'm supposed to be. I love the idea of twisting the porn isekai premise into a Doki Doki thing, it's a cool idea and led to some genuine emotional moments, the graveyard visit hitting me particularly hard as I lost a friend last year. However, I'm at a particularily grindy point where some of the lewd stuff is unlocked for some girls and when I got hit with Miku's freakout in the locker room scene and I guess I'm wondering if there really is no separation between the paths I'm led down, because "Will you still think she's pretty when all of it falls out?" feels pretty personally directed at anyone trying to fap to the game. Yumi and Mayu or wtvr her name is are clearly fucked up paths, and after they asked me to leave them alone I did, but it looks like if you just want to fap you're shit out of luck cause either way you force yourself on Yumi.

Anyways my point is, since this is clearly a long game, should I put my dick away and follow the creepy existential path because I'm stuck doing it either way? If that's the case I'm fine with it but there was a clear separation and amount of choice in the matter and slowly the choices are being ripped away and now every sex scene has this creepy looming threat that at any moment you're gonna be shamed for it, so I guess I'm just wondering from the dev's perspective if me trying to stick to the lewd stuff before enjoying the horror story is possible or if I should come back to this without the dick out, because that will make the grinding much more boring I think. It had a good balance before but now not so much, scenes are mixing and there really isn't any choice anymore except to find the next horror trigger.

I like it a lot but the amount of grinding you have to do for affection is grossly disproportionate to what I think is the intended story no matter which girls you go for. If that story is the ultimate goal, the sex parts need to be trimmed, unless I'm meant to feel shame so the horror aspects have more impact in which case mission accomplished, I'm conflicted. Otherwise it's just a half and half that kinda loses both my boner and my engagement in the story by committing so hard to both.

Since there are a lot of theories being thrown around on what the world actually is, i'll add my humble opinion on this.

The whole time i'm getting the feeling that the world MC is in, is not actually a world at all. The way i see it, the whole area, being Kumon-mi, is an artificially made up space created by god God to amuse themselves. First probably without anyone from outside sphere, but later, he started plucking people from the real world, which have a peculiar personality, which he injected into this space to observe how things would turn out, especially in the lewd department. I would say that (as Maya once said), this world works on a cycle, with variables in form of Sensei eventually swapped out for a new person, once the previous one gets stale and predictable. I don't think MC is the first person to be put in Kumon-mi, and most likely won't be last. He is just another interesting specimen to try out.

Now speaking of Maya, there are a lot of ways anyone can go about her. I myself lean closest to the option that she started out as the rest of the girls, resetting after each time. Until one point, when she became aware of the reset itself, which in my opinion is yet another of decisions of Kumon-mi's creator to make things fresh and interesting. I think that she has seen myriads of senseis up to the point that the story is taking place, and understandably being bored by things being repeated so many times, with only little changes, depending on which iteration of sensei is currently present. That's how she knows the outcomes for the most part, because each sensei is guided along the pre-made paths with pre-made outcomes, only changing on the order of them happening and some being avoided as a whole. The only truly unique experiences for her is her own interaction with the versions, as they may act without total control of options presented by god God for once.

Now aside from those two things, there is one more that keeps bouncing in my mind, and that is if Selebus eventually takes this a step further and pulls a Monika on us with Maya catching a whiff that sensei is not even in control of his own actions, and it's actually god God giving the metaphorical reins to a person that's sitting in the front of the computer, us. And with it going even more into the chain of used and being used as there would be a line of
god God (who made the world and is observing the actions with the intent of amusement, only to swap out the subjects once he gets bored) -> the player (who controls sensei and his actions) -> sensei (who got plucked from his own world after his suicide and who thinks is controlling the body of another person) -> person that formally was sensei until used as a body for god's God's shenanigans.
Now throw in Maya somewhere in the middle with the potential of realization about the whole exchange of power and we got a pretty spicy soup of confusion.
Not to mention there's still space for Selebus himself to casually drop an "actually, i, the author, created the god and the world, made him seemingly be in charge and the only real person ever besides me is the player in charge of sensei" and let Maya catch a whiff of that to completely destroy any sense of reason, logic and grasp of reality (or multiple realities at that manner) the poor girl might have... or had.

Anyways my point is, since this is clearly a long game, should I put my dick away and follow the creepy existential path because I'm stuck doing it either way? If that's the case I'm fine with it but there was a clear separation and amount of choice in the matter and slowly the choices are being ripped away and now every sex scene has this creepy looming threat that at any moment you're gonna be shamed for it, so I guess I'm just wondering from the dev's perspective if me trying to stick to the lewd stuff before enjoying the horror story is possible or if I should come back to this without the dick out, because that will make the grinding much more boring I think. I like it a lot but the amount of grinding you have to do for affection is grossly disproportionate to what I think is the intended story no matter which girls you go for. Otherwise it's just a half and half that kinda loses both my boner and my engagement in the story by committing so hard to both.

spoilers.title: What is the world, really?
spoilers.html:
The whole time i'm getting the feeling that the world MC is in, is not actually a world at all. The way i see it, the whole area, being Kumon-mi, is an artificially made up space created by god God to amuse themselves. First probably without anyone from outside sphere, but later, he started plucking people from the real world, which have a peculiar personality, which he injected into this space to observe how things would turn out, especially in the lewd department. I would say that (as Maya once said), this world works on a cycle, with variables in form of Sensei eventually swapped out for a new person, once the previous one gets stale and predictable. I don't think MC is the first person to be put in Kumon-mi, and most likely won't be last. He is just another interesting specimen to try out.

Now speaking of Maya, there are a lot of ways anyone can go about her. I myself lean closest to the option that she started out as the rest of the girls, resetting after each time. Until one point, when she became aware of the reset itself, which in my opinion is yet another of decisions of Kumon-mi's creator to make things fresh and interesting. I think that she has seen myriads of senseis up to the point that the story is taking place, and understandably being bored by things being repeated so many times, with only little changes, depending on which iteration of sensei is currently present. That's how she knows the outcomes for the most part, because each sensei is guided along the pre-made paths with pre-made outcomes, only changing on the order of them happening and some being avoided as a whole. The only truly unique experiences for her is her own interaction with the versions, as they may act without total control of options presented by god God for once.

Now aside from those two things, there is one more that keeps bouncing in my mind, and that is if Selebus eventually takes this a step further and pulls a Monika on us with Maya catching a whiff that sensei is not even in control of his own actions, and it's actually god God giving the metaphorical reins to a person that's sitting in the front of the computer, us. posts.content_html_raw:
Does this game really create a message on Discord every time someone starts the game? It looks that way to me, but I'm not a Python programmer.

Here's some code from the beginning of script.rpy:
Code: 
init -20 python:
    import discord_rpc
    import time

    def readyCallback(current_user):
        print('Our user: {}'.format(current_user))

    def disconnectedCallback(codeno, codemsg):
        print('Disconnected from Discord rich presence RPC. Code {}: {}'.format(
            codeno, codemsg
        ))

    def errorCallback(errno, errmsg):
        print('An error occurred! Error {}: {}'.format(
            errno, errmsg
        ))
python:
    # Note: 'event_name': callback
    callbacks = {
        'ready': readyCallback,
        'disconnected': disconnectedCallback,
        'error': errorCallback,
    }
    discord_rpc.initialize('739939315643318282', callbacks=callbacks, log=False)
    start = time.time()
    print(start)
    discord_rpc.update_connection()
    discord_rpc.run_callbacks()
    discord_rpc.update_presence(
        **{
            'details': 'Main Menu',
            'start_timestamp': start,
            'large_image_key': 'mayasweep2'
        }
    )
    discord_rpc.update_connection()
    discord_rpc.run_callbacks()

return

That brings up a potential key word there, proper. Is it possible to mess it up bad enough to leave such a scar and not kill the person? Since you choose to focus ONLY on a kidney removal, rather than MORE likely operations, let me go into detail. Kidney removal from the front (ventral, or belly) would entail (intact) removal of basically the entire mid and lower gastrointestinal tract, then cutting through a rather thick membrane to just EXPOSE the kidney, excise it, then replacing the gi tract WITHOUT rupturing it and creating a whole shitload (probably literally!) of more problems, then suturing up the wound. I don't think OUR technology could do it that way, especially when the easier, simpler, preferred method is to go in from the back. My nephew had a kidney transplant and my mother and older sister both died from kidney failure, so I do know what I'm talking about.

Once again, drop the kidney idea. There are other, much better explanations for a ventral scar like the one shown.

Don't ignore the signs, take some time to be selfish.

Look after yourselves everyone.

The game is going to be quite long, with the dev (Selebus) confirming multiple endings including bad ends, "purity route" ends with each main girl, and a true ending.

No ending is in the game yet, as it's actually fairly early in development still.

Personally, I'm happy it's going to be long. The character writing is phenomenal, and I love the slow buildup to things happening with each of the characters. Big character developments are foreshadowed long in advance, but its often only likely to be picked up on if you're familiar with what that character's going through or in hindsight.

If what you meant by "doesn't look too good" is the prospect of a happy harem ending, yup. This is a denpa game. Think Higurashi or Doki Doki Literature Club.
Hell, one of the main characters has already commited suicide (two if you count whoever the person inside Sensei's body used to be), and as I've said, we're pretty early in development.
I wouldn't expect the first ending we get to be a happy one.

alex2011 said:
I think the warning is fine as is, though it wouldn't hurt to make it more explicit to cover his back. As far as being flippant, I mean, it is still just a game even with those topics. What do you mean by the 'face your fears is better suited to a horror game' part? I don't quite get that line. If you mean as the title, the horror is a major element, but this is still basically a dating sim, so that wouldn't work. Let me know if I interpreted that line wrong, I'm genuinely interested in your meaning there.
Click to expand...
I'm going to preface this comment by saying that this is not a hill I intend to fight and die on, it really doesn't matter that much to me. Ultimately either Selebus sees my comment, agrees and tweaks the warning, or he sees it, disagrees and does nothing. There are more important hills.

I had intended to go no further than my original comment but as you have specifically asked me to explain I will. I really don't want to shit the thread up with a discussion about trigger warnings though (which funnily enough tend to trigger people).

You have definitely misunderstood my comment. Currently the warning states that "as in real life, horrible things may happen" then goes on to say "face your fears".

It is this final line that I was referring to as flippant.

The reason I say this is that usually I'd expect such a phrase to refer to more visceral fears - the dark, spooooooky ghosts, the unknown, blood and guts i.e. generic horror.

In a straight up generic horror setting this would be entirely appropriate. The ghosts (or whatever) aren't real, they aren't going to hurt you and it is through them that we experience catharsis.

But Selebus is pushing in to some really heavy topics regarding mental ill health and the very real consequences of that.This to me is starting to butt up against the boundaries of what would usually be lumped into the "horror" genre, particularly in games. Indeed I struggle to think of any mainstream games that really seek to address these issues, perhaps Silent Hill?

I would accept that "horrible things" does in fact include the kind of topics that are being explored. But I'm not sure it's a simple as facing one's fears when addressing them.

You specifically mention being more explicit to help him in covering his back but I think this really misses the point of content warnings and ascribes a really cynical motivation to Selebus. Given the very genuine style of his writing and engagement I don't think that's a fair assessment of his motivation for including such a warning given that he didn't have to include any warning at all.

I have found as I have gotten older and worked through my own issues that I have mellowed on the concept of trigger warnings, which I never used to like. To me, giving your audience a heads up that "hey we're going to be talking about some fucked up shit" is just a way of showing respect for that audience and hurts noone.

I suppose a parallel can be drawn with the medical warning immediately preceding the content warning in question. This is a photosensitive epilepsy warning. Very few people would begrudge such a warning despite it being virtually redundant. Why should we treat mental health differently?

So the point, if any is to be found in the rambly nonsense above, is that on the one hand Selebus is addressing some serious stuff in a serious and respectful way, but begins that by undermining his approach a little.

Tl;Dr snowflake got triggered

posts.content_html_raw:
Cerpin said:
I'm going to preface this comment by saying that this is not a hill I intend to fight and die on, it really doesn't matter that much to me. Ultimately either Selebus sees my comment, agrees and tweaks the warning, or he sees it, disagrees and does nothing. There are more important hills.

I had intended to go no further than my original comment but as you have specifically asked me to explain I will. I really don't want to shit the thread up with a discussion about trigger warnings though (which funnily enough tend to trigger people).

You have definitely misunderstood my comment. Currently the warning states that "as in real life, horrible things may happen" then goes on to say "face your fears".

It is this final line that I was referring to as flippant.

The reason I say this is that usually I'd expect such a phrase to refer to more visceral fears - the dark, spooooooky ghosts, the unknown, blood and guts i.e. generic horror.

In a straight up generic horror setting this would be entirely appropriate. The ghosts (or whatever) aren't real, they aren't going to hurt you and it is through them that we experience catharsis.

But Selebus is pushing in to some really heavy topics regarding mental ill health and the very real consequences of that.This to me is starting to butt up against the boundaries of what would usually be lumped into the "horror" genre, particularly in games. Indeed I struggle to think of any mainstream games that really seek to address these issues, perhaps Silent Hill?

I would accept that "horrible things" does in fact include the kind of topics that are being explored. But I'm not sure it's a simple as facing one's fears when addressing them.

You specifically mention being more explicit to help him in covering his back but I think this really misses the point of content warnings and ascribes a really cynical motivation to Selebus. Given the very genuine style of his writing and engagement I don't think that's a fair assessment of his motivation for including such a warning given that he didn't have to include any warning at all.

I have found as I have gotten older and worked through my own issues that I have mellowed on the concept of trigger warnings, which I never used to like. To me, giving your audience a heads up that "hey we're going to be talking about some fucked up shit" is just a way of showing respect for that audience and hurts noone.

I suppose a parallel can be drawn with the medical warning immediately preceding the content warning in question. This is a photosensitive epilepsy warning. Very few people would begrudge such a warning despite it being virtually redundant. Why should we treat mental health differently?

So the point, if any is to be found in the rambly nonsense above, is that on the one hand Selebus is addressing some serious stuff in a serious and respectful way, but begins that by undermining his approach a little.

Tl;Dr snowflake got triggered
Click to expand...
Remember that this is a Denpa game, a common comparison game being Doki Doki Literature Club, which is also a Denpa game and also deals with very real issues in the same manner. Remember the scenes with Yuri and Sayori, those are very real issues and there is nothing addressing them as the real life issues they are in that game. Silent Hill is a traditional horror game, not a Denpa game. I don't think Selebus meant to face the fear of these topics, but to face the fear these topics coming up as suddenly as they do in this game can induce. I had forgotten where it said that since I haven't played from the start for a while, which is why I asked.

I mention making the warning more explicit as a precaution because there are some people out there who would take issue with the way it is now. They would completely gloss over the fact that there is indeed a warning to say that it isn't enough. I'm not trying to paint Selebus or the motivation to upgrade the warning as cynical, that's just a suggestion to make sure he doesn't run into that kind of trouble because that type of group can be a real pain to deal with. As I said, personally, I believe the warning is adequate as it is now, but some may not believe the same. Yes, the epilepsy warning does have very little use at the moment, but once again, it is better to be safe than sorry. There is no difference in the way the two are treated, he is very aware how serious both are and he is addressing them as such. Because I don't think he meant what you think he meant in the sections you think undermine his approach, I don't think he is undermining his approach at all. In fact, if one were to actually play the game and see the events, I am in no way saying or implying you haven't just to put that out there, they would see just how accurately he is portraying these very real issues.

If you need an example, definitely look at Rin. She is exactly what I picture when thinking of someone dealing with her issues and it actually scares me to consider that this fictional character isn't the only one going through such horrors, even though I was already aware it happens in real life, but that many very real people are as well, some of which have taken the ultimate and irreversible final step or who have caused permanent damage that they will live with until their time comes naturally.

Just wanted to chime in without replying to anyone as I see there was/is a lengthy discussion about mental health and how it relates to this game.

The “Face Your Fears” message is not an attempt to undermine that or make light of it. It’s exactly the opposite. I believe that the best way to combat the struggles real people face in life is to attack them to head on. We can not simply shy away from things that make us feel upset or uncomfortable or any other negative adjective that could be swapped in for one of those.

When I say “Face Your Fears,” I mean the fear of death. I mean the fear of loss. I mean the fear of rejection. I mean every “real” fear that people have.

I write things like this to help overcome my own mental struggles. All of these characters are reflections of different parts of me. I just also think many people may benefit from diving into the darkness in order to pull out some light when they can’t find any in other places.

I figured there was some real experience behind that writing, it was just way too real to not come from experience. You are absolutely correct on every point you covered and this could not have been said any better. The only way we will ever overcome these things is to confront them ourselves as the people suffering their effects and I do believe that having someone to relate to, even if fictional, can help to do just that. I've faced the fear of loss, the fear of rejection, and even the fear of death multiple times in multiple different scenarios that I have not mentioned here. Hell, I just stared death in the face a couple weeks ago and won, medical issues that I won't go into detail about, but that did almost kill me and this isn't the first time that has happened in the last two years, it's at least the third. The fear of rejection has been by me for most of my life from high school to now. It cost me my first love and several opportunities as a musician that I know damn well I could have made happen. It was two little words with great power that made me fail in both, what if. What if she said no and we couldn't go back, what if I screwed up and became the laughing stock of my entire local music community. The fear of loss has been with me since day one because of family that was constantly in and out of my life because of their own bad decision and is more prominent now than it has ever been because people I hold dear are at an inevitable precipice, one neither they nor I have the power to turn them away from. I am happy to report that you are succeeding with at least one person by sharing this so that 'people may benefit' with it. I myself am not going through depression, but I am a bit of a loner when it comes to my own problems, so I rarely ever seek help for them unless it is blatantly obvious I cannot handle it alone. It's more of a fierce independence than anything. The connections I have made to your characters and the very real effect this game and no other is having on me showed me that I was wrong and merely subconsciously refused to see it. I thought I had a handle on it and I clearly did not or I wouldn't still feel the effects of my own experiences in these subjects. The connections I have made to your characters are the deepest I have ever made. I'm not just the same as them, I AM Chika in that I have dealt with my own father leaving when I was little, multiple times. I AM Futaba in that I was bullied, psychologically mostly, but physically as well (Yumi's interactions with her can be taken as bullying even if her intent is actually to help Futaba). So, with all that said, there is but one thing left to say. Thank you, Selebus. Thank you for this glorious work of art, this masterpiece in the making. Thank you for the assistance I didn't even know I needed. Thank you for everything you have done with this project from the bottom of my heart I sometimes jokingly refer to as pitch black or evil because of my usual preferences in adult materials being a fake portrayal of what would be a crime that would do terrible things to the victim if done for real. I'm starting to feel like my subscription and praise aren't enough, but that's because they really aren't. I couldn't possibly ever thank you enough, but I'll think of something to at least try, count on it. Assuming you're fine with the use of subscriber benefit materials like the cards you provide to us at the $10 tier, a fan project might be in order. I've never done something like that, so this will be a first and it might be a little rough in quality. Yes, I am officially asking permission just to do something as a thank you even if I don't necessarily have to.

spoilers.text: I figured there was some real experience behind that writing, it was just way too real to not come from experience. You are absolutely correct on every point you covered and this could not have been said any better. The only way we will ever overcome these things is to confront them ourselves as the people suffering their effects and I do believe that having someone to relate to, even if fictional, can help to do just that. I've faced the fear of loss, the fear of rejection, and even the fear of death multiple times in multiple different scenarios that I have not mentioned here. Hell, I just stared death in the face a couple weeks ago and won, medical issues that I won't go into detail about, but that did almost kill me and this isn't the first time that has happened in the last two years, it's at least the third. The fear of rejection has been by me for most of my life from high school to now. It cost me my first love and several opportunities as a musician that I know damn well I could have made happen. It was two little words with great power that made me fail in both, what if. What if she said no and we couldn't go back, what if I screwed up and became the laughing stock of my entire local music community. The fear of loss has been with me since day one because of family that was constantly in and out of my life because of their own bad decision and is more prominent now than it has ever been because people I hold dear are at an inevitable precipice, one neither they nor I have the power to turn them away from. I am happy to report that you are succeeding with at least one person by sharing this so that 'people may benefit' with it. I myself am not going through depression, but I am a bit of a loner when it comes to my own problems, so I rarely ever seek help for them unless it is blatantly obvious I cannot handle it alone. It's more of a fierce independence than anything. The connections I have made to your characters and the very real effect this game and no other is having on me showed me that I was wrong and merely subconsciously refused to see it. I thought I had a handle on it and I clearly did not or I wouldn't still feel the effects of my own experiences in these subjects. The connections I have made to your characters are the deepest I have ever made. I'm not just the same as them, I AM Chika in that I have dealt with my own father leaving when I was little, multiple times. I AM Futaba in that I was bullied, psychologically mostly, but physically as well (Yumi's interactions with her can be taken as bullying even if her intent is actually to help Futaba). So, with all that said, there is but one thing left to say. Thank you, Selebus. Thank you for this glorious work of art, this masterpiece in the making. Thank you for the assistance I didn't even know I needed.
